feature: Oil paint carries and smears colour, with bristle ridges
summary: The Oil Paint brush now paints like a loaded bristle brush: thick streaked strokes with ridges that catch the light, colour picked up from paint it crosses and dragged on past it, and a brush that runs dry along a long stroke.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. A blank canvas (File, New, Image).

try.do: Press B, then pick Oil Paint from the Medium menu over the tool bar.
Drag a stroke down the canvas in black.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pick a blue from the colour swatch at the end of the tool bar and drag a stroke across the black one.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Zoom in on the crossing (Command +) and look just past it, where the blue carries some black on.
Drag one long stroke right across the canvas and watch it break into dry streaks near the end.
Open the stroke sheet to compare Smear 0, 40 and 100 and Load 20, 70 and 100 side by side.

evaluate: Does a stroke read as thick paint laid by a brush, rather than a flat fill?
Crossing a stroke, does the colour drag along about as far as a real brush would at the default Smear?
Does the brush run dry at about the right distance at the default Load, or should a full brush go further?
Is the light on the ridges strong enough to see at 100% zoom, or too strong up close (the close-up sheet)?
rough: Load and Smear have no control in the tool options yet; they are set from their defaults (70 and 40) until the settings slice (each-brush-shows-its-own-settings-in-the-tool-op) gives every medium its own rows.

Zoomed in past about 140%, the bristles go softer when the button comes up: the renderer bakes a paint layer covering a 12 megapixel canvas at about one pixel a point. Folded into painting-keeps-up-with-the-pointer-on-a-12-megap.

Pickup reads only the paint layer the stroke lands on, never the screenshot under it, so painting over a picture does not smear the picture (the house's non-destructive rule, docs/design/brushes.md decision 2).
The walk can only pick black and one plain blue, so its crossing shows black carried into blue (a darkening); the sheet shows red into blue, which reads far better.
No mock covers an oil stroke's look; where the Brush and its Medium menu sit is unchanged from the slice that built them.

Pictures: walk captures are real windows (Screen Recording granted, screen unlocked), photographed behind another app; the close-up is a crop of 2026-10-25-oil-paint-2-smeared-sc.png. Measures in 2026-10-25-oil-paint-measures.txt.
